name: Side-Lying Thoracic Rotation
pose: Side-lying open-book rotation with knees stacked and top arm opening behind
accessibilityLabel: Side-lying thoracic rotation with hips and knees bent together, lower arm forward and upper arm opened behind as the chest turns upward.

Exercise: SIDE-LYING THORACIC ROTATION, open-book phase. Lie on RIGHT side on floor with right side pelvis and right outer thigh supported. BOTH hips and knees bent roughly90degrees with KNEES STACKED TOGETHER on floor in front of pelvis; legs remain stacked while chest rotates. Lower RIGHT arm straight out on floor in front at shoulder height, palm up. Top LEFT arm opens in opposite direction behind body and rests near floor at shoulder height, palm up. Chest turns gently upward toward ceiling, head follows left hand without strained neck, hips remain side-lying. No forced shoulder range; top arm can hover slightly if needed. Elevated side-three-quarter view from foot side shows both arms, chest rotation and stacked knees clearly. Coral only visible thoracic back musculature if exposed; chest/abdomen/arms grey; do not color hidden muscles through torso. Highlights represent mobilized region. Full figure with all limbs, no equipment.
